pr_title: Fix OpenAPI server URLs for Aspire scenarios
pr_body:
## Description

This PR supports respecting he X-Forwarded-Proto and X-Forwarded-Host headers when generating server URLs in OpenAPI documents. When these headers are present in the request, the OpenAPI document service will use them to generate the correct server URLs instead of using the original host and scheme values derived from the service configuration.

This is particularly useful in environments where the API is behind a proxy, load balancer, or gateway, allowing the generated OpenAPI document to correctly reference the public-facing URL rather than the internal service URL.

Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/57332

## Customer Impact

Without this change, documents served behind reverse proxies or forwarded endpoints do not reflect the correct service URl, particularly impact for the ASP.NET Core + Aspire scenario. While the issue is easy to workaround, we want a smoother experience with Aspire out-of-the-box.

## Regression?

- [ ] Yes
- [X] No

## Risk

- [ ] High
- [ ] Medium
- [X] Low

Low-risk, becase change as it only affects the generation of server URLs in OpenAPI documents and does not impact the actual API functionality.

issue_context.title: Server URLs in OpenAPI document are incorrect when application used with .NET Aspire
comments:
As a workaround, you can fix this by using [my OpenAPI Extensions library](https://github.com/martincostello/openapi-extensions?tab=readme-ov-file#usage):

```csharp
builder.Services.AddOpenApiExtensions(options => options.AddServerUrls = true);
```

This should take into account the forwarded headers and should map to the correct URLs - [code](https://github.com/martincostello/openapi-extensions/blob/98c10f06f0c118673d0b48ff9d909460ec59f285/src/OpenApi.Extensions/Transformers/AddServersTransformer.cs#L37-L61).

As another workaround, the servers defined in the OpenAPI document can be overridden to an empty array:

```csharp
app.MapScalarApiReference(_ => _.Servers = []);
```

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e4a46d47-c943-424f-8aa0-4b59586972c2)

> As another workaround, the servers defined in the OpenAPI document can be overridden to an empty array:
> 
> app.MapScalarApiReference(_ => _.Servers = []);

Nice! - that worked - Thanks

I have the same issue, is there still no solution?

I'm using `OpenAPI` + `Swashbuckle.AspNetCore.SwaggerUI`
We’re going to need to do something here to fix this.

> app.MapScalarApiReference(_ => _.Servers = []);

This workaround from @boulc did the trick for me, but it shouldn't be that difficult. Especially in docker deployments the url is totally irrelevant and after reverse proxying I somehow expected this to work out of the box with Forwarded Headers configured.
Using @martincostello nuget package (Thank you) but watching the outcome of this with baited breath as this is really important to us.

review_comments:
The array initialization syntax is incorrect. Replace ["http://localhost:5000"] with a valid C# array initialization such as new[] { "http://localhost:5000" }.
```suggestion
            new OpenApiTestServer(new[] { "http://localhost:5000" }));
```

The syntax used for initializing the list is invalid. Replace the '[.. addresses.Select(...)]' syntax with a valid C# list initialization such as addresses.Select(address => new OpenApiServer { Url = address }).ToList().
```suggestion
            return addresses.Select(address => new OpenApiServer { Url = address }).ToList();
```
